note: SIMULATED paperwork only: this register names threats and the slices that build their controls. No entry claims a control is built until that slice banks with tests.

threats.impact: A fake node advertises capabilities it does not have, attracts tasks (including sensitive ones), and returns fabricated or no results while polluting placement decisions.

mitigations.control: Per-node keypairs and mesh-root-issued node certificates; a node is its key, not its claimed id
Mutual TLS on every fabric channel; no plaintext mode exists
Every fabric message signed by its node; unsigned or wrongly-signed traffic dropped and counted

threats.name: Node impersonation
threats.residual_risk: A stolen node key impersonates that node until the operator revokes it; revocation and key custody (Kista, Y-196) remain operator duties.

threats.asset: correctness of answers delivered to callers
threats.impact: A node returns plausible but wrong, biased, or fabricated results; consumers act on them and Urdr fitness memory learns from lies.

mitigations.control: Mandatory provenance on every result (node, engine, model, quant, timings); an answer without a receipt is not a mesh answer
Per-kind verification contracts and invariant checking before delivery; violations quarantined, never silently passed
Shadow verification of critical tasks on a second node/model; disagreement is a preserved event, resolved by declared rules
Anomaly flags and quarantine policy for nodes whose results suddenly change shape

threats.name: Poisoned results
threats.residual_risk: Two colluding nodes can agree on a wrong answer; verification raises cost and evidence, it does not create truth. Low-criticality tasks accept single-node results by design.

threats.asset: fabric bandwidth, node CPU, and registry convergence
threats.impact: A flooding node drowns honest state propagation, exhausts small nodes (Pi-class), and can eclipse quieter nodes from the registry view.

mitigations.control: Per-node rate and size quotas on gossip and tasks; flooding nodes throttled by their peers
Signed messages with provenance, so spam is attributable to one key and one quota
Fabric observability: message rates and drops visible on the operator's door

threats.name: Gossip and heartbeat spam
threats.residual_risk: A Sybil crowd of distinct keys could each stay under quota; at local scale membership is operator-issued (Y-011), so Sybil resistance rests on issuance discipline. WorldNet scale is Y-215/Y-224 research, NOT PROVEN.

threats.asset: executing nodes, their data, and their engines
threats.impact: A task that is secretly code, an exfiltration request, a resource bomb, or a prompt crafted to leak another caller's context could compromise the executing node or its scopes.

mitigations.control: Tasks are data, never code, unless a signed task kind explicitly says so
Bounded execution sandbox: time, token, and output limits; cancellable; no ambient authority beyond the task's declared scopes
Urdr privacy scopes enforced at read inside the store, not by caller good intentions
Sensitive task kinds have their provenance chain checked link by link
Encrypted payloads for sensitive task kinds, sealed to the executing node

threats.name: Malicious tasks
threats.residual_risk: Prompt-level attacks against a model (jailbreaks, context extraction via crafted inputs) cannot be fully prevented by the fabric; scope enforcement limits what a successful attack can reach.

threats.impact: A node serves a backdoored or corrupted quant under a trusted model's name; every result from it is suspect and fitness data rewards the impostor.

mitigations.control: A model is present only when its hash verifies against the registry entry
Model fetch is hash-verified end to end when policy allows peer fetch
Failure shape 'model corrupt' detected, contained, and reported distinctly from engine errors

threats.name: Tampered or poisoned model files
threats.residual_risk: A correctly-hashed but maliciously trained model is indistinguishable by hash; behavioural detection belongs to Skuld anomaly work (Y-132) and is graded, not guaranteed.

threats.asset: confidentiality of prompts, contexts, and results
threats.impact: Prompts and results often carry the household's private work; a passive listener harvests them, and metadata alone reveals who asks what, when.

mitigations.control: TLS everywhere on the fabric with node certificates; no plaintext fallback
Payload encryption for sensitive task kinds, sealed to the executing node
Privacy audit: packet-level proof a local task never leaves the LAN unencrypted, or at all, per its policy

threats.name: Eavesdropping and traffic analysis on the LAN
threats.residual_risk: Endpoint compromise defeats transport encryption; traffic timing/volume metadata remains visible to a LAN observer even with TLS.

threats.asset: node availability, thermals, and mesh responsiveness
threats.impact: Expensive but well-formed tasks saturate queues, force model swaps, or cook a small node; critical work starves behind casual bulk.

mitigations.control: Resource governor: per-node memory/thermal/CPU ceilings with graceful refusal before damage
Priority and fairness shares per caller; the operator's work preempts by standing priority
Muspelheim shedding by criticality when the mesh saturates; deferred work remembered as temporal debt

threats.name: Resource exhaustion by legitimate-shaped load
threats.residual_risk: A determined caller with valid scopes can still consume their fair share at inconvenient times; fairness bounds starvation, not annoyance.

threats.asset: Urdrs graph: decisions, outcomes, contexts, fitness
threats.impact: Forged outcomes steer future placement toward bad nodes; poisoned contexts leak into other callers' tasks; false facts replicate by CRDT before anyone notices.

mitigations.control: Provenance law: every fact carries its source (node, task, time); unsourced assertions cannot enter Urdr
Contradictions coexist with sources; consumers choose by trust policy, Urdr never silently picks a winner
CRDT merge correctness property-tested; partition healing reconciles by task id, never double-answers
Forgetting and deletion propagate through replicas and are themselves facts

threats.name: Registry and memory poisoning
threats.residual_risk: A trusted-but-wrong source produces well-provenanced false facts; provenance makes lies attributable and removable, not impossible.

threats.asset: exactly-once task semantics and caller budgets
threats.impact: A captured or duplicated task runs twice: wasted capacity at best, double side effects or double answers at worst.

mitigations.control: Task id is the task's only name; duplicates reconciled by id, never double-answered
Store-and-forward entries carry a TTL; expiry is an event, not a silence
Signed, channel-bound messages make off-path replay detectable

threats.name: Replay and duplicate execution
threats.residual_risk: At-least-once delivery inside a partition remains possible; reconciliation guarantees one delivered answer, not one execution.

threats.asset: mesh root key, node keys, and operator authority
threats.impact: Whoever holds the mesh root or a node's private key is that authority; a lost laptop or a phished operator silently becomes the mesh's enemy inside.

mitigations.control: Node keys kept via Kista where the node supports it; nodes without Kista use a protected local store and say so
Audit tap is off by default, loud when on, and operator-consented only
Security audit by attack attempts before release; findings fixed or roaded with owners

threats.name: Operator-door abuse and credential theft
threats.residual_risk: No protocol survives an operator who hands over the root key; the design limits blast radius (per-node keys) but cannot remove the human factor.
